newsitem.title: UK: P&O venture picked for Bombay container port.
newsitem.headline: P&O venture picked for Bombay container port.

text.p: British-based shipping and construction group Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) said on Tuesday a joint venture firm in which it is a partner had been chosen as prefered bidder for a $200 million port project for the Nava Sheva harbour, Bombay, India.

It said in a statement it hoped the decision would soon lead to a licence agreement being signed, under which it would be entitled to reclaim the site, then build and operate a fully equipped container terminal under a 30-year concession contract.
"The total joint venture investment over the period of the project is estimated at $200 million and will be funded by a combination of equity and third party debt," P&O said.
It named the other principal partners in the project as Malasyian logistics and transport group Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd and DBC Port Management, part of Bombay's largest stevedoring group.
The plan is to complete the new container terminal, with a 600-metre-long quay, in 2000 and give it an annual capacity to handle more than 600,000 teus (20-foot equivalent units).
The terminal would be managed by P&O unit P&O Ports, while construction development would be managed by another group company, Bovis Construction.
Container traffic has grown through Bombay's two ports at an annual rate of more than 16 percent since 1980, P&O added.

P&O has long experience in port development in fast-growing parts of the world and last year strengthened its own presence in the global container shipping trade by forming a joint liner venture with Dutch Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV.
